name: Familial Hyperthyroidism Due to Mutations in TSH Receptor
aliases: Hereditary Hyperthyroidism due to TSHR Mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Non-Autoimmune Hyperthyroidism

criteria.description: Identification of activating mutation in the TSH receptor gene (TSHR)
Clinical and biochemical evidence of hyperthyroidism without autoimmune markers
Presence of hyperthyroidism in at least two first-degree relatives consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Absence of thyroid autoantibodies (e.g., anti-TPO, anti-thyroglobulin, TSH receptor antibodies)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical hyperthyroidism with family history plus genetic confirmation of TSHR activating mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of autoimmune thyroid disease is essential to differentiate from Graves' disease.

laboratory: Elevated free T4 and free T3 levels
Negative thyroid autoantibodies (anti-TPO, anti-thyroglobulin, TSH receptor antibodies)
imaging: Thyroid ultrasound showing diffuse gland enlargement without nodularity
Radioactive iodine uptake scan showing increased uptake diffusely
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of hyperthyroidism

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse radioactive iodine uptake with autoimmune markers
Presence of multiple thyroid nodules on imaging
Localized increased uptake on radioactive iodine scan

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe hyperthyroid symptoms suggesting thyroid storm
Atrial fibrillation or other serious cardiac arrhythmias
Severe muscle weakness or paralysis indicating thyrotoxic periodic paralysis
references: Refetoff S, et al. Familial non-autoimmune hyperthyroidism due to TSH receptor mutations. Endocr Rev. 1993;14(3):324-338.
Orphanet: Familial hyperthyroidism due to mutations in TSH receptor (ORPHA:424)
Mullis PE. Genetic causes of hyperthyroidism. Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2000;14(2):295-310.
